subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should route/ACP bindings become a supported tool-access security boundary with `tools.allow` and `tools.deny`, or should operators use existing group, sender, session, and agent policy surfaces instead?
rationale: This adds a new public config and authorization surface whose precedence overlaps existing policy layers, so automation should not choose the permanent security model.

options.title: Design Binding Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Use Existing Policy Surfaces
options.body: Decline the new binding key and document group/channel, sender, session, and per-agent policy as the supported tool restriction path.

options.title: Defer To Conversation Identity
options.body: Block this on the broader scoped conversation identity/capability design if maintainers want one authorization model instead of a binding-specific slice.

recommendation.title: Design Binding Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across policy pipeline and scoped group-policy code plus related security/product discussion.
